chapter_theme: The kinds of mudra: shambhavi, khechari, the grace-hand and the knowledge-mudra are distinguished, and the highest seal is the mudra of silence, in which speech and mind both cease and release is gained; the chapter ends by placing Vedanta and Siddhanta together in pure Saivam.
structure_note: Silence and release open the chapter (1892). The named mudras are listed and glossed (1893, 1894, 1897), silence is defined (1895, 1896), the yogi's attainments gathered (1898), pure Saivam defined (1899), and the mudras assigned to kinds of people (1900). 1901 closes on coloured paths.

1892.reading: When the four-sevens cease, the mudra attained is fixed in the speech of silence, and saved at the holy feet of supreme Nandi, with all tumult gone, one gains good release.
1892.nuance: நாலேழு may be twenty-eight, or four and seven; what ceases is not said, perhaps the senses and faculties or the tattvas. பாலான மோன மொழி is the 'speech' of silence, a paradox the chapter returns to.

1893.reading: The three turiyas become the place of closing; restraining there the hard-to-utter sound, shambhavi and khechari join, and the truth is knowledge growing: these are the distinct mudras.
1893.nuance: துரியங்கள் மூன்று (three fourth-states), சொருகு இடம் (the place of closing or inserting) and உரைத்தாரம் are technical and obscure. Shambhavi (gaze fixed within) and khechari (the tongue turned up, moving in space) are named mudras of yoga.

1894.reading: Shambhavi is Nandi's gracious glance; the grace-hand mudra is free of births; khechari is the truth that rises in practising Om; and the knowledge-mudra is the true knowledge of the Lord we practise.
1894.nuance: The verse reads each mudra as an inner reality rather than a posture: the gaze becomes the Lord's glance, the gesture of the hand his grace. அருட்பாணி may be the hand gesture of grace or the grace of the Lord's hand.

1895.reading: Within the station he becomes Sadasiva, within knowledge he is the good Sivam; so the mudra of silence, in which the form of Sivam otherwise seen is hidden, is release beyond release.
1895.nuance: தானம் may be a yogic station or a place of worship; ஏனைச் சிவமாம் சொரூபம் is unclear. முத்தாந்த முத்தி, the release at the end of release, is a Siddhanta phrase for the final state.

1896.reading: When speech and mind are both still, that is silence; if only speech falls silent, one is merely mute; the pure are those in whom speech and mind are silent, and who knows the purity they bring about?
1896.nuance: The verse separates mauna from muteness (மூங்கை): silence of the tongue alone is nothing. The last line may also be read 'who can know that pure state which makes them?'

1897.reading: The mudra of yoga is the eight siddhis; considering the mudra of knowledge that is one, Veda-khechari and shambhavi are fitting; for yoga, khechari is the yoga mudra.
1897.nuance: The verse sorts mudras by path, yoga and knowledge, but the assignments in lines 2 and 3 are compressed and the term வேத கேசரி is unclear.

1898.reading: The yogi, the eight siddhis, the sound of grace, the traces of past impressions, the enjoyer, his intellect, the good path of the aims of life, the good shakti and the testing of the supports: seeing them as one, he reaches the One and stands.
1898.nuance: The verse is a list of terms (வாதனை for vasana, புருடார்த்தம் for the human aims, ஆதார சோதனை for examining the bodily supports) whose links are not stated. The point seems to be that all are gathered into one vision.

1899.reading: The twelvefold path and the sixteenfold path, the ten kinds that end desire and the six limbs, the unfailing nature of Vedanta and Siddhanta, considered together with the nine Agamas: that is pure Saivam.
1899.nuance: துவாதசம் (twelve) and கோடசம் (sixteen) may be the paths of breath reaching twelve and sixteen finger-breadths, or kalas. நவாஅகமோடு is read as the nine Agamas Tirumular names elsewhere, but நவ may also mean new. The verse makes pure Saivam hold Vedanta and Siddhanta together.

1900.reading: The mudra of silence is the seal of the liberated, the mudra of knowledge the seal of the lords, the mudra that sweetens is the Siddhanta mudra, and the mudra that is displayed belongs to the religion seen outwardly.
1900.nuance: தேனிக்கும் and கானிக்கும் are obscure; they are read here as 'makes sweet' and 'is shown', which ranks inner mudras above those seen in a sect's practice. The ranking is my reading of the sequence, not stated.

1901.reading: The trace seen on the pure path rises in the middle; the flower path seen there stands as the golden place; the higher path seen is the white moon's land; and the one who has seen the blue path becomes the Spotless One.
1901.nuance: The four paths, pure, flowered, higher and blue, are coloured stages of yogic ascent through the central channel, but which centres or lights they name is not fixed by the verse. நின்மலன் may be the Lord or the yogi who becomes like him.

links.note: 1893 names shambhavi and khechari among the mudras; 1894 says what each one is: the Lord's glance, and the truth that rises with Om.
Both put the mudra of silence highest: 1895 calls it release beyond release, 1900 the seal of the liberated.
The Kural says whatever else one fails to guard, one should guard the tongue; Tirumular says guarding the tongue alone only makes one mute, and silence is true only when the mind is still too.

source_issues: 1896: line 4 reads சுத்த்ததை, with a doubled consonant; read சுத்தத்தை.
1893: உரைத்தாரம் and சொருகுஇடன் are obscure and may be corrupt.
